title: An immersed constructible stratum of an affine scheme splits into finitely many affine constructible pieces
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\iota:Z\to X$ be an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose image $E=\iota(Z)$ is a constructible subset of $X$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Then there are a finite set $K$ (possibly empty), affine schemes $Z_k$ and immersions $\kappa_k:Z_k\to Z$ ($k\in K$) such that each composite $\iota\circ\kappa_k:Z_k\to X$ is an immersion, its image $E_k=\iota(\kappa_k(Z_k))$ is a locally closed [def-weil-locally-closed-subset] and constructible subset of $X$, the sets $E_k$ ($k\in K$) are pairwise disjoint, and $E=\bigcup_{k\in K}E_k$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0 (lemma-etale-stratified-finite), proof, line 12049: 'After refining the partition further we may assume $X_i$ affine as well' (the refinement step stated without proof)

proof.text: Reduction to $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Since $X$ is affine there are a commutative ring $A$ and an isomorphism of schemes $\varphi:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An isomorphism is an open immersion onto the whole target [def-weil-open-immersion], hence an immersion (with the identity as closed immersion) [def-weil-closed-immersion], and so is $\varphi^{-1}$; compositions of immersions are immersions [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). Hence $\iota'=\varphi\circ\iota:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an immersion. The underlying map of $\varphi$ is a homeomorphism, so it maps open sets, quasi-compact open sets, hence retrocompact open sets, closed sets, finite unions, intersections and complements to the same kind of sets; therefore $\varphi$ maps constructible subsets [def-weil-constructible-subset] and locally closed subsets [def-weil-locally-closed-subset] of $X$ bijectively onto those of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and preserves disjointness and unions. In particular $\iota'(Z)=\varphi(E)$ is constructible. If $(Z_k,\kappa_k)_{k\in K}$ satisfy the conclusion for $\iota'$ with images $E'_k$, then $\iota\circ\kappa_k=\varphi^{-1}\circ(\iota'\circ\kappa_k)$ is an immersion (composition again) with image $E_k=\varphi^{-1}(E'_k)$, and the $E_k$ are locally closed, constructible, pairwise disjoint with union $\varphi^{-1}(\varphi(E))=E$. So we may and do assume $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\iota$ an immersion with constructible image $E$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0, proof, line 12049 (the step is stated without proof there); Schemes, Lemma Tag 02V0 (composition of immersions)

proof.text: Disjoint basic pieces. Since $E\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ is constructible, it is a finite union $E=B_1\cup\dots\cup B_m$ of basic sets $B_j=D(f_j)\cap V(g_{j,1},\dots,g_{j,n_j})$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-constructible-basic-union]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-basic-sets-disjoint-refinement] there are finitely many pairwise disjoint basic sets $C_k=D(f_k)\cap V(g_{k,1},\dots,g_{k,n_k})$, $k\in K=\{1,\dots,p\}$ ($p=0$, $K=\emptyset$, allowed, e.g. when $E=\emptyset$), with $E=\bigcup_{k\in K}C_k$. Put $E_k=C_k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0G1P (lemma-constructible), line 5434; the disjoint refinement is the refinement step of Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0, line 12049

proof.text: The pieces are images of immersions of affine schemes. For $k\in K$ let $J_k=(g_{k,1},\dots,g_{k,n_k})$, $R_k=(A/J_k)_{\bar f_k}$, $W_k=\operatorname{Spec}R_k$ and $w_k:W_k\to X$ the morphism induced by $A\to A/J_k\to R_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-basic-subset-immersion-image], $w_k$ is an immersion and $w_k(W_k)=D(f_k)\cap V(g_{k,1},\dots,g_{k,n_k})=E_k$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00F8 (lemma-constructible-is-image), lines 5467-5471, with Lemmas Tag 00E4 and 00E5

proof.text: Definition of $Z_k$ and $\kappa_k$. Let $Z_k=Z\times_XW_k$ be the fibre product of $\iota$ and $w_k$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $\kappa_k:Z_k\to Z$ and $q_k:Z_k\to W_k$, so $\iota\circ\kappa_k=w_k\circ q_k$. The projection $\kappa_k$ is the base change of the immersion $w_k$ along $\iota$, hence an immersion; the projection $q_k$ is the base change of the immersion $\iota$ along $w_k$ (the fibre product is symmetric in its two factors), hence an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (1).

$Z_k$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] (with $f=\iota$, $g=w_k$, $P=Z_k$, $q=q_k$), $q_k(Z_k)=w_k^{-1}(\iota(Z))=w_k^{-1}(E)$, and $w_k^{-1}(E)=W_k$ because $w_k(W_k)=E_k\subseteq E$ (steps 2, 3). So $q_k$ is an immersion whose image $W_k$ is closed in $W_k$, hence a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (1) to $q_k$ and the affine open $V=W_k=\operatorname{Spec}R_k$ of $W_k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the scheme $Z_k=q_k^{-1}(W_k)$ is affine.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion); Schemes, Lemma Tag 01JT (points of fibre products), used through the cited node

proof.text: Conclusion. For $k\in K$, $\iota\circ\kappa_k=w_k\circ q_k$ is a composition of immersions (steps 3, 4), hence an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e), and its image is $w_k(q_k(Z_k))=w_k(W_k)=E_k$ (steps 3, 5). Each $E_k=D(f_k)\cap V(g_{k,1},\dots,g_{k,n_k})$ is the intersection of an open and a closed subset of $X$, hence locally closed [def-weil-locally-closed-subset], and is constructible, being a (one-term) finite union of basic sets [lem-weil-pbc-affine-constructible-basic-union]. The $E_k$ are pairwise disjoint and $E=\bigcup_{k\in K}E_k$ by step 2; each $Z_k$ is affine by step 5. This is the assertion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_affine_immersion_constructible_pieces {X Z : Scheme} (hX : IsAffine X) (ι : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion ι] (E : Set X) (hE : E = Set.range ι) (hEc : IsConstructible E) : ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Fintype K) (Zk : K → Scheme) (κ : ∀ k, Zk k ⟶ Z) (Ek : K → Set X), (∀ k, IsAffine (Zk k)) ∧ (∀ k, IsImmersion (κ k)) ∧ (∀ k, IsImmersion (κ k ≫ ι)) ∧ (∀ k, Set.range (κ k ≫ ι) = Ek k) ∧ (∀ k, IsLocallyClosed (Ek k)) ∧ (∀ k, IsConstructible (Ek k)) ∧ (Set.PairwiseDisjoint Set.univ Ek) ∧ E = ⋃ k, Ek k
